the structure of the 5’→3’ exoribonuclearase (Xrn1) shows the active site and four additional domains (D1-D4) that stabilize the N-terminal segment.
the 510-residue extension of Xrn1, which is absent from Xrn2, contains four domains that stabilize the N-terminal domain and might interact with protein partners of the enzyme.

the structural basis of Xrn1 function.
the molecular mechanisms that control the activity and the function of Xrn1, which is essential for the survival of eukaryotic organisms.
the structure and function of the 5'→3' exoribonuclearase Xrn1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the K. lactis Xrn 1 is similar to the structure of the yeast rat1, with the addition of a 510 amino acid long C-terminal extension.

Xrn1 has four domains, D1–D4, which are not present in Rat1/Xrn1, but are required to stabilize the N-terminal segment, which contains the catalytic core of Xrn1.

the 5′ to 3′ exorinucleases (Xrn1 and Xrn2) are composed of a catalytic core domain and an auxiliary segment.

the 510-residue domain is a unique feature of Xrn1 and that its presence is essential for the activity and stability of the enzyme.
